title: Nine Microns Wide
subtitle: 生命科学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）
meta: 主题语境：生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）　|　核心词汇：cell　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cell 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 my mother was sent to count ① cell she could not see, and she said the counting was the whole of the lesson. The ② cell, meaning the unit and not the body, was nine microns wide and was counted by whoever came last; cell, she said, is the only thing in a body that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cell in that body had the same wall, and the ④ cell at the end, meaning the one the researchers kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted properly. Cell, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cell was the whole of the organism, meaning the life it carried and not the unit. The ⑥ cell, meaning the life and not any of that, is the only thing in an organism that everybody studies and nobody questions; cell, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both a unit and a life. She said the life is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ cell had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the wall. The ⑧ cell of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine microns and eleven years of counting; cell, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cell I remember is the one at the end, which was counted in 1969 and is still described as the smallest in the county. A ⑩ cell, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being counted; every cell, she said, is a life that has agreed to look like a unit. She said the life was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 细胞（指那个单位本身，与整个身体相对）
C. 固定搭配：count a cell 数一个细胞
D. n. 细胞（指身体里每一个）
E. n. 细胞（指末尾那一个）
F. n. 细胞（抽象：它承载的那份生命）
G. n. 那份生命（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The cell, meaning the unit and not the body
cell was the whole of the organism
the cell had become a number in a report
The cell of the whole thing
A cell, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: count a cell 意为“数一个细胞”，1947 年母亲被派去数她看不见的那个细胞。
cell 意为“细胞”，指那个单位本身而不是整个身体，宽九微米，由最后来的人计数。
cell 指身体里每一个细胞，每一个都是同样的细胞壁。
cell 指末尾那一个（研究人员保留的那一个），是唯一有人认真计数过的。
cell 意为“细胞”，抽象指它承载的那份生命，父亲说 cell 就是那个生物体的全部。
cell 为抽象用法，指那份生命本身，是一个生物体里人人都研究、却没人质疑的东西。
cell 意为“细胞”，到 1964 年这个 cell 成了报告里的一个数字。
cell 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九微米和十一年的计数。
cell 意为“细胞”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1969 年数过，至今仍被说成全县最小的。
cell 为抽象总称，祖母说一个细胞是唯一会因为被认真计数而变好的东西。
